page: Amazon Web Services m7i.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and fourth-generation Intel Xeon 8488C processors. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 48 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 24 physical cores running at 3.2 GHz, supplemented by 105 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 192 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 5 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual CPU. The instance does not bundle local disk storage and includes no discrete graphics processing units. Network throughput is provisioned with a 19 Gbps baseline, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

The underlying Intel processor implements Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) alongside AVX-512, targeting machine learning and vectorized mathematical routines. Synthetic and execution benchmarks place the platform consistently within upper tiers. It records a PassMark CPU score of 63240.19, a Geekbench single-core score of 2010.0, and a multi-core score of 16969.0. Matrix extensions significantly benefit CPU inference workloads, yielding 351.99 text generation tokens per second on small 135M models to reach top-decile performance. Extended instruction and encryption benchmarks register 61238.73 and 51341.08 points in PassMark respectively, alongside a Clang compilation score of 39723.0.

Memory subsystem testing reveals uncached large-block 256 MB reads of 179.25 GB/sec and writes of 84.16 GB/sec, falling within median industry ranges despite the high DDR5 frequency. A primary architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent data transactions require network-attached storage across the 19 Gbps network interface. Given its density of 48 dedicated compute threads and DDR5 memory, the instance delivers high resource efficiency for non-accelerated vector computations without requiring GPU hardware. It is suited for relational database operations, high-throughput Redis caching, CI/CD compilation, static web serving, and mid-scale machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i.12xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance equipped with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8488C processor providing 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores clocked at 3.2 GHz and 192 GB of DDR5 memory. The server maintains a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio, a 19 Gbps network baseline, and features Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions, while excluding local storage and dedicated GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate upper-quartile performance across PassMark CPU (63240.19), Geekbench multi-core (16969.0), and Redis SET operations (63.12 million ops/sec), alongside top-decile generation speeds for small-model LLM inference (351.99 tokens/sec). Conversely, uncached memory bandwidth registers within the median range. Without bundled NVMe storage, persistent data relies entirely on networked storage volumes. The instance provides balanced compute and memory capacity for enterprise database servers, in-memory caching layers, code compilation pipelines, web serving fleets, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
